title: Playing with Lee Collins at the Victory Club
summary: Lovett's band sat in with Lee Collins at the Victory Club on North Clark Street, where Sweet William and Freddie Flynn played.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: G-E-R-O-U-L-D. And then I started a question, but I guess I laid you off a little bit. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Were there other New Orleans men that you remember having played with around Chicago? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Well, Lee Collins. Did we mention him? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. No, we haven't. And you said that you have a photograph of your band with Lee Collins.
G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Yes, I have with Bill Price and all those fellas playing with Lee Collins at the Victory Club, which was on North Clark Street. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. We used to go down there quite a lot.
G-E-R-O-U-L-D. It seemed to me that if anybody could sit in, there weren't many restrictions. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. That's right, yeah. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. So, Lee had what? Three, four pieces?

G-E-R-O-U-L-D. It was himself and there was a piano player named Sweet William, I believe. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Yes. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Actually, I think his name was William Sweet. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Oh, oh. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Yeah, but everybody used to call him Sweet. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. And I don't know if he had a regular drummer there or not.

G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Freddie Flynn? Do you remember that? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Yes, I remember the name. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Freddie Flynn, frequently drummed for him. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. All right, I'd like to stop this for a moment. . . . . Thank you.
